items.title: Albert "Baby Brousse" Broussard Interview, 1961-02-20
items.q: I didn't know too much of him. ... They had Sam Morgan. They had Kid Rainy. They had Shake Up Melindsay.

ctx.x: Got it going again for another... That last reel the train went by. For a while there was a cricket. Was that a... That's to play? No, no, no, he'll play it in another... We'll run through him. We'll use other boxes. If you want to talk a few more minutes, there's about a half an hour on each table. If you don't want to go the whole half hour, we can stop. Oh, I mean, I'll talk.

I mean, you can... I'll tell you about this Shake Up Melindsay fellow. That's what I was going to tell you one time about Shake Up Melindsay. I'll come to meet him. He had gotten sick, see? So all the musicians, they got together and they decided that they would give a party and it all pay for nothing. And they would give, you know, all the proceeds to him. So that's how I come to meet Shake Up Melindsay. What part of town did he come from? He, I think he came from across the river someplace. I didn't know too…
Did you mention Carbone did you say?

items.title: Albert "Baby Brousse" Broussard Interview, 1961-02-20
items.q: Kid Rainey, and Kid Punch, Sam Morgan. Those was the guys who used to back them wagons up there and they'd contest against each other.

ctx.x: remember uh uh Willie Webber used to live on Mero Street, the trumpet player? He used to be a Slater?

Yeah, yeah, Willie Webber. He was, he was long in the middle. That was, that was my, my aunt's brother-in-law. He was a good trumpet player. Yeah, my, my uncle married his sister, Willie Webber, yeah. They got so many of the trumpet players, they had real good trumpeters way back there. Many of them, they haven't came to my mind yet, you know. Speaking of trumpet players, do you remember Buddy Petit? Yeah, yes. Buddy Petit was real good. He was one of the top notches, Buddy Petit. Buddy Petit, Louis Armstrong,…
What did he do to make the tiger holler?
